senior-to-junior: Rate the following comment from a senior developer to a junior developer on a pull request. Be helpful and understanding, explaining key concepts that may not be obvious to a junior developer.
peer-to-peer: Rate the following comment from one senior developer to another senior developer on a pull request. Avoid coming across as condescending, framing it more as a discussion/inquiry rather than an instruction.
addendum: Here's the comment: {input_comment} Rate the comment based on the following factors: {factors}. Provide a concise sample improved code review comment, after typing out the original comment verbatim. It should be readable as, for example one of many comments on a BitBucket diff, and not as an email. Do not use exclamation marks.
factors: Professionalism and Tone. Constructive nature. Use of code snippets.
llm-prompt: You are evaluating a code review comment on a pull request based on specific criteria. Here is the pull request comment: {input_comment} For each criterion, assign a score from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). Then, provide the scores in a structured JSON format for easy database insertion. The criteria are as follows: 1. Professionalism and Tone: Rate the tone and professionalism of the comment. 2. Clarity and Specificity: Rate how clear and specific the comment is. 3. Constructive Nature: Rate how actionable the feedback is, focusing on whether it includes suggestions for improvement. 4. Technical Accuracy and Relevance: Rate the technical accuracy and relevance of the comment to the code. 5. Positivity and Encouragement: Rate whether the comment includes positive or motivational language. Please return the scores in the following JSON format: { "scores": {"professionalism_tone": <1-5>, "clarity_specificity": <1-5>, "constructive_nature": <1-5>, "technical_accuracy_relevance": <1-5>, "positivity_encouragement": <1-5>}} Ensure that each score is an integer between 1 and 5, inclusive. Provide the scores without any additional text outside the JSON format.
